paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: we don't do good to get saved. We do good BECAUSE we're saved. Paul says God saved us, "not by the righteous deeds we had done, but according to His mercy" (Titus 3:5). Read that again, because it means nobody gets to show up at God's door with a résumé.

Paul also says that at one time we too were "foolish, disobedient, misled" (Titus 3:3). That's why he wants believers to be gentle and to malign no one (Titus 3:2). When you remember what mercy did for you, it's hard to look down your nose at the next person. I know a little about being pulled out of the back of a drawer, and let me tell you, it makes a stamper humble real fast.

So what does a saved person do? Paul says to "devote themselves to good works in order to meet the pressing needs of others" (Titus 3:14). He says it so they will not be unfruitful, and he says these things are "excellent and profitable for the people" (Titus 3:8). Mercy first, then good work. Now get out there and BAKE, friend, because grace was never meant to just sit on the counter.
